thread:
noah: FYI I hit a racey auth issue in the Python AsyncClient when mixing REDWOOD_API_KEY env var and passing api_key explicitly. Caused our multi-tenant worker to send requests with the wrong tenant key.

noah: minimal repro:
```py
# export REDWOOD_API_KEY=env_key
from redwood import AsyncClient

client = AsyncClient(api_key="tenant_specific_key")
await client.chat.complete(...)  # ends up using env_key
```

noah: observed behavior: logs show "auth: selected env key" and sometimes an AttributeError in auth wrapper. stack: 
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "handler.py", line 48, in on_event
    await client.chat.complete(...)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood/client/async_client.py", line 88, in chat
    headers = await self._auth.get_headers()
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood/auth.py", line 23, in get_headers
    key = _module_env_key or self._explicit_key
AttributeError: 'AsyncAuthWrapper' object has no attribute '_explicit_key'
```

jana: thanks for reporting. sounds like the auth wrapper isn't always setting the instance-level key and some module-level state is read at import time. Is this reproducible in pytest with asyncio.gather?

noah: yes. I wrote a test that spins up 6 tasks, each constructing AsyncClient with different keys — about half the tasks send with the wrong key.

alex: this is similar to a bug we fixed in the sync client a while back where REDWOOD_API_KEY was cached globally. Two ideas: (1) make env read lazy and per-instance, (2) accept a provider/callable for api_key so rotation is easier.

jana: agree. small design notes: the api_key parameter should accept Union[str, Callable[[], str], Callable[[], Awaitable[str]]]. Internally the client/auth layer should coerce that into an async provider and call it for each request (or wrap with a cache if user opts in). We should also document that passing a provider may be called frequently unless they use caching TTL.

noah: typing pain: if we widen param types we need to update stubs so mypy and pyright don't complain. We can define an APIKeyProvider Protocol with both sync and async call signatures and provide a helper decorator to wrap sync providers.

alex: implementation plan:
- Remove module-level env read. Read os.getenv in Auth.__init__ or get_headers (lazy) and prefer explicit provider result over env.
- Ensure AsyncAuthWrapper always stores explicit value (or provider) on the instance to avoid AttributeError.
- Add support for sync/async provider and a small LRU/TTL cache util in auth with optional token_cache_ttl param.
- Add unit tests: concurrent client creation, sync provider, async provider, TTL caching semantics.

jana: can you also add a migration note: any code that relied on module import to freeze REDWOOD_API_KEY will now see env read lazily. Might affect init-time behavior for serverless cold starts.

noah: I'll open a draft PR with failing test attached. Would prefer a patch release because this blocks tenant rollouts.

ci-bot: Created issue RN-2781: "AsyncClient env fallback race + api_key provider support" and linked draft branch: gh/redwood/sdk/async-auth-fix.

alex: thanks. once PR is up ping @sdk-reviewers. target: 0.8.5 patch if tests pass. I'll add a brief docs snippet showing a vault-backed async provider and example caching decorator.

noah: one extra ask: please don't change sync client surface area or default behavior — keep backwards compatibility.

jana: we'll keep sync parity. I'll include compatibility tests for sync client reading env var and passing explicit key.

noah: tl;dr: bug where AsyncClient may use env key instead of explicit api_key when multiple clients are created concurrently. Fix: lazy env read, store per-instance provider, support sync/async providers, optional caching TTL.
